steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Spatial planning considers how people move through and use spaces — function, flow and atmosphere are key.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Scale drawing uses set ratios (1:50, 1:100) to represent spaces accurately; orthographic projection shows plan, elevation and section.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Architectural models communicate 3D ideas that drawings cannot — they reveal spatial relationships, light and material qualities.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Responding to site means understanding the context: existing structures, landscape, climate, culture and community.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring architectural and interior design. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with architectural and interior design. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with architectural and interior design. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to architectural and interior design, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refine | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
